children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Home services platform Urban Company posted a net loss of 183 crore for the July-September period, up over threefold from 59 crore in Q2FY26. The ballooning of the company's loss happened on the back of elevated spending to compete in the buzzy instant househelp business.

For the second quarter of this fiscal, operating revenue grew 41% year-on-year to 537 crore. The company's board, on October 16, also approved a plan to raise 2,500 crore. When the company went public in September 2025, it had raised 472 crore. Urban Company's cofounder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal, speaking at the post earnings analyst call, said that InstaHelp's losses will remain elevated for many quarters to come. "We are building for scale, not near-term profits," he said, adding that from Q3FY28, its core business profits will fund InstaHelp losses.

On the proposed fundraise, Bhal said, "Should the competitive intensity in InstaHelp rise, we have both the balance sheet and the intent to respond in full." In a letter to shareholders, the Gurugram-based company said it had 1,901 crore in cash as of September 30, while its businesses excluding the InstaHelp segment generated 119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the past nine months. "The purpose of the raise is flexibility. The business today is materially larger than at the time of listing, and growth has stepped up meaningfully.

We now operate three businesses at scale, with proven economics across India Core, International and Native," the company said. "The raise gives us the ability to invest with conviction across each of these areas: to sustain higher growth in the core business, to fund the next phase of growth in Native, to cement leadership in InstaHelp through its most competitive phase, and to pursue inorganic opportunities selectively," it added.

Urban Company reported a 41% year-on-year rise in operating revenue to 537 crore for the July-September quarter. Its net loss, however, tripled to 175 crore as continued cash burn in InstaHelp weighed on its bottom line. InstaHelp under pressure With competition in the instant househelp segment remaining intense, Urban Company's post-discount average order value (AOV) fell to 118 in the September quarter from 134 in the June quarter. "Competitive intensity remained high, and we leaned further into new user acquisition, where introductory pricing is lower," the company said in the letter. "We regard this as the cost of building habit while the category is being formed, not as the steady-state price of the service.

In the medium term, we believe net order value should move up for us, albeit slowly and subject to competitive intensity. As it does, loss per order should improve further," it added. Urban Company competes with Nexus Venture Partners-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto in the instant househelp segment.

title: Urban Company's Loss Triples to 183cr
